classification.difficultyReason: Convert one day into twelve decay periods and apply the geometric term formula with correct initial-term indexing.

content.prompt: Every two hours, half of a particular medical isotope decays. If there was originally 20 grams, how much remains after a day (correct to two significant figures)?

answer.worked:
One day contains $24\div2=12$ two-hour periods. The initial mass is the first term, so the mass after twelve periods is the thirteenth term.

$$\begin{align*}a&=20,\qquad r=\frac12\\a_{13}&=ar^{13-1}\\a_{13}&=20\left(\frac12\right)^{12}\\a_{13}&=\frac{20}{4096}\text{ g}\\a_{13}&=0.0048828125\text{ g}\\a_{13}&\approx4.9\times10^{-3}\text{ g}\quad\text{(2 significant figures).}\end{align*}$$
